subject: Risk & Compliance
title: WeWork: Governance by Ego
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on WeWork: Governance by Ego.

hook.text: Adam Neumann charged WeWork $5.9 million in rent for buildings he personally owned. The board let him.

buildup.text: WeWork gave Neumann near-total control through super-voting shares and a hand-picked board.

discovery.text: The IPO prospectus revealed rampant self-dealing. The valuation collapsed from $47 billion to $8 billion.

twist.text: SoftBank's Masayoshi Son had invested $10 billion without demanding standard governance protections.

climax.text: WeWork proved that no amount of growth excuses unchecked power. Governance is not optional.

punchline.text: $47 billion to $8 billion. Ego without governance.

quiz.question: What governance problem plagued WeWork?
options: The founder had near-total control and rampant self-dealing
